open_points.subject: Create replay after an ordinary correction
open_points.text: This holds while the record the first create made keeps its values
open_points.question: Does changing any value of a Project or Customer by a normal correction end replay recognition for its original create request, or does recognition survive until the record is erased or anonymised?
options: Any correction ends recognition, so replaying the original create may create a new record.
Corrections do not end recognition; the stored create request id continues to identify the original record.
Only removal of the facts needed for recognition, as in erasure or anonymisation, ends recognition.
open_points.default_guess: Recognition survives ordinary corrections and ends only when erasure or anonymisation removes the create request id.

witness.initial: Customer C was recorded with request id R and phone P1; C retains R under M04.
events: The owner corrects C's phone to P2.
The owner repeats the original record-customer create with request id R.
outcomes: Registry recognises R and does not create another Customer.
Because C no longer keeps its original values, Registry treats the repetition as a new create and mints Customer C2.
witness.observer: The owner, who sees whether a second Customer exists.

open_points.subject: Project create replay after whole deletion
open_points.text: Erasing a customer or anonymising a project removes everything that would tell a repeat ...; a create repeated after that is a new create
open_points.question: What happens when a project-create request is repeated after the first project was deleted whole rather than anonymised?
options: The repeat is a new create because deletion also removed every fact that could identify the earlier request.
Replay recognition survives outside the deleted Project, so the repeat does not create a project.
The repeat is refused because the earlier project was deleted.
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a new create because the whole record and its create request id are gone.

witness.initial: Project P was created with request id R, then archived.
events: The owner confirms deletion of P whole.
The owner repeats the original create request R.
outcomes: Registry mints a new project because no replay evidence remains.
Registry recognises or refuses R despite deletion and creates no project.
witness.observer: The owner and consumers, who see whether a new project identity exists.

open_points.subject: Meaning of “a create” after customer erasure or project anonymisation
open_points.text: a create repeated after that is a new create
open_points.question: Is this exception limited to repeating the create of the erased Customer or anonymised Project itself, or does it also apply to other create actions whose records or parents were affected, especially room creation?
options: Only the create of that same Customer or Project becomes a new create.
Every affected create, including a room create whose room disappeared with an anonymised project, becomes a new create.
Other creates retain their normal preconditions and replay rules; for example, a room retry on an anonymised project is refused.
open_points.default_guess: Limit the exception to the create of the Customer or Project whose replay evidence was removed; other create actions retain their normal preconditions.

witness.initial: Active project P has room Q, created by agent session S with request id R.
events: The owner archives and anonymises P, removing Q.
Kernel for S repeats the add-room request R.
outcomes: Reading “a create” broadly, Registry performs a new create and mints another room.
Reading it as limited to the anonymised Project's own create, Registry refuses the room action because P is archived/anonymised and creates no room.
witness.observer: The owner or Kernel, which sees a new room versus a refusal.
